key_insight: DFT-derived stacking-fault energy landscapes enable reliable PFDD predictions of Cu–Al stacking-fault widths, while landscapes from the tested classical and machine-learned potentials cause premature partial-dislocation pinning.
engineering_relevance: Accurate alloy deformation modelling requires potentials that reproduce the shear-energy landscape, not just lattice parameters and elastic moduli.
method: Compare generalized stacking-fault energy surfaces from DFT, classical embedded-atom ZW, and machine-learned GAP methods.
Incorporate each energy surface into phase field dislocation dynamics (PFDD) simulations.
Evaluate equilibrium stacking-fault widths across Al contents against standalone MD and available experimental values.
evidence_signal: Despite reasonable agreement in lattice parameters and elastic moduli, both potentials deviate substantially from DFT at characteristic energy-surface points; DFT-driven PFDD predicts widths that increase with Al content and agree with standalone MD and pure-Cu experiments.
watch_item: Experimental agreement reported in the abstract is limited to pure Cu, so validation across Cu–Al compositions remains important.
paper_title: Phase field dislocation dynamics prediction of stacking fault widths in Cu-Al Alloys using generalised stacking fault energy from DFT and interatomic potentials
